title: Citation: A Key to Building Responsible and Accountable Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: As a position paper, it does not conduct empirical measurements. It theoretically evaluates citation bias (the uneven representation or over-reliance on certain types of sources) and proposes future methodologies for measuring it, such as developing evaluation techniques to quantify residual bias in model outputs and assessing the impartiality of retrieval mechanisms.

Conceptually evaluated through illustrative examples (e.g., analyzing the statement "Women are better suited for caregiving roles than men") to demonstrate how integrating citations can attribute biased claims to original sources rather than the language model's intrinsic beliefs. No empirical measurement is conducted.
